 Cuba, Guyana, Guadeloupe earn big League B victories
 11/12/2026 - 11:48 PM share-facebook share-x share-whatsapp share-copy-link Guyana Goes Five for Five  Goals galore in League B as Cuba, Guadeloupe and Guyana post big wins. 
 MIAMI – The 2026/27 Concacaf Nations League continued on Thursday with League B Group Stage action, highlighted by convincing victories for Cuba, Guyana, and Guadeloupe.
 Cayman Islands 0-6 Guyana
 Guyana secured a 6-0 shutout of the Cayman Islands in Group A at Leonora National Track & Field Center in Leonora, Guyana.
 Omari Glasgow got things started for Guyana by converting a penalty in the 5’.
 Morgan Ferrier extended the lead for the Golden Jaguars in the 12’ with a finish from inside the box to capitalize on a ball from the left.
 Osaze De Rosario added a third for Guyana from the penalty spot in the 39’.
 Stephen Duke-McKenna then netted a brace with goals in the 42’ and the 48’.
 Nathan Ferguson scored the sixth and final strike for Guyana in the 50’.
 Guyana secured its fifth victory in five matches, leading Group A with 15 points. Cayman Island is third with 1 point.
 Barbados 0-3 Guadeloupe
 Guadeloupe defeated Barbados 3-0 in Group B at Stade Roger Zami in Le Gosier, Guadeloupe.
 Claudio Beauvue found the opener for Guadeloupe in the 10’.
 Ange-Freddy Plumain extended the lead for Guadeloupe in the 41’, collecting a ball played over the top in space before dribbling past a defender and striking from inside the box.
 Substitute Jonathan Gamby sealed the victory with a goal in the 80’.
 With this win, Guadeloupe secured its second victory in five matches and reached 7 points, 3 behind the leader, Barbados, which sits at 10 in Group B.
 Bonaire 1-7 Cuba
 Cuba earned a 7-1 victory against Bonaire in Group C at Estadio La Polar in La Habana, Cuba.
 Michael Camejo opened the scoring in the 7’ to place Cuba in the lead.
 Jorge Aguirre doubled Cuba’s lead in the 51’ with a powerful right-footed volley from inside the box.
 Yunior Pérez added a third for Cuba in the 56’.
 Myron Bostdorp scored Bonaire’s sole goal of the match in the 58’.
 Cuba then scored two goals in quick succession, with Daniel Díaz finding the back of the net in the 69’ and Luis Paradela in the 74’.
 Diaz then sealed his brace in the 77’ with a left-footed strike from inside the box following a ball over the top.
 Didier Reinoso rounded out the result for Cuba with a strike in the 79’.
 With this result, Cuba reaches 11 points and sits in first place in Group C, while Bonaire is third with three points.
